extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO OED/disciplinary staff, and legal professionals involved in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, describing the procedural requirements for notice, opportunity to respond, determination when no response is filed, publication requirements, and notification to other disciplinary bodies and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline may request imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a State authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; a Notice and Order is sent to the respondent advising of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice and Order was sent by certified mail notifying Respondent that the OED Director had filed a Complaint requesting that the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the State (here, the Supreme Court of Virginia opinion). The Notice provided an opportunity to file a response opposing imposition within forty (40) days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity and time to oppose reciprocal discipline (40 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is given forty (40) days from delivery of the Notice and Order to file a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state, based on the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was delivered on July 31, 2023; respondent must file within 40 days to raise objections under § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to timely respond waives the opportunity to oppose on those grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may oppose imposition of identical discipline by asserting one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references § 11.24(d)(1) as the statutory basis for possible opposition but does not restate those reasons; a respondent must invoke the statutory grounds within the 40‑day response period to prevent automatic reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond: no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the OED Director (or delegated authority) may determine that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and that imposition of the reciprocal discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter, Respondent did not file a response, and the Final Order states that, 'In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact ... and reprimanding Respondent is the appropriate discipline.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand as appropriate reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate under the reciprocal-discipline rules, the USPTO may publicly reprimand a registrant for misconduct that was the basis of state discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: 'Respondent is hereby publicly reprimanded.' The reprimand mirrors the state action that was the predicate for the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED's FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are made publicly available for review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room; the Final Order must be published there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette consistent with template
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the notice text provided in the Final Order (a Notice of Public Reprimand describing the registrant, registration number, the rule violated, predicate state discipline, and related conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order provides a specific notice text to be used (or materially consistent wording) including the registrant's name and registration number, description that discipline is for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), a summary of the state reprimand (including the Virginia Rule violated and probation conditions), citation to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, and the FOIA URL where the disciplinary decision is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs dissemination of the notice and reasons for discipline beyond USPTO publication to appropriate state agencies and courts to ensure other jurisdictions are informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and mailing requirements for Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at the most recent address provided to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a) and to addresses where the OED Director reasonably believes the respondent receives mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Certificate of Service in the Order certifies mailing to specified addresses (including the respondent's home and law office) and to the USPTO address; compliance with mailing/service rules is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate state-law misconduct and conditions that can inform USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary findings (here: a Virginia public reprimand and probation for violating Virginia Rule of Professional Conduct 1.7(a)(2) for engaging in sexual relations with a client) serve as the factual predicate for USPTO reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order summarizes the state discipline (including probation conditions: take and pass the MPRE and complete 250 hours of community service, with potential suspension for failure to comply) as the basis for imposing USPTO discipline under the reciprocal-discipline framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for disciplinary action (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's disciplinary action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, which authorize reciprocal discipline and the Office's procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly cites these statutory/regulatory authorities and notes that disciplinary decisions are publicly available at the OED FOIA Reading Room.
